title: Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang as CEO Just 11 Days After His Exit
yt_title: Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang as CEO Just 11 Days After His Exit
yt_description:
Nvidia's board has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, only 11 days after he left the company amid reports about his private life. Interim CEO Colette Kress goes back to being CFO, a petition for his return passed 180,000 signatures, President Trump said there is no national security risk, and Nvidia shares jumped at the open. SEC and Justice Department investigations into Nvidia are still underway.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! The biggest boss in AI chips is back in the big chair. On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective immediately. Just eleven days ago, on November twelfth, Huang left the company he co-founded. He stepped away after reports about his private life, including an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. While he was gone, finance chief Colette Kress ran Nvidia as interim CEO. Now she goes back to being CFO. But the exit did not go quietly. A petition to bring him back passed one hundred eighty thousand signatures. Silicon Valley insiders pushed hard, and Al Jazeera reports even Elon Musk signed it. According to the Associated Press, the board's vote to bring him back was unanimous. Board chair Harvey Jones said Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia. Huang says he returns with, quote, the greatest humility and renewed commitment. President Trump cheered the move, saying the government sees no national security risk in Huang's return. And Wall Street? Al Jazeera says Nvidia shares jumped more than thirty three percent as markets opened. Hold on to your graphics cards! Analyst Dan Ives had warned that Nvidia could lose as much as thirty percent of its value without him. But this is not over. Investigations into Nvidia by the SEC and the Justice Department are still underway. So: the leather jacket is back, the stock is up, and the big questions are still open.
